title: Induced/Incomparable versus Ramsey
summary: We consider the following problem: Let $H$ and $F$ be two graphs on $k$ vertices and assume $F \neq H$. We say that $H$ and $F$ are incomparable if neither $F$ nor $H$ contains the other. Let $H$ be a graph on $k$ vertices and let $G$ be a graph on at least $k$ vertices. Then $G$ is said to be $H$-exact if any induced subgraph of $G$ on $k$ vertices is either isomorphic to $H$ or incomparable with $H$. Exact($H$) is the family of all graphs $G$ which are $H$-exact.
